newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa engine firm ADE in 400mln rand Cuban deal.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa engine firm ADE in 400mln rand Cuban deal.

text.p: South African diesel engine manufacturer Atlantis Diesel Engines (ADE) said on Monday it had concluded a 400 million rand deal with Cuban government agency Unecamoto which looks after transport in the sugar industry.
In terms of the deal, ADE -- based in Atlantis near Cape Town -- would supply Unecamoto with 10,000 diesel engines for commercial use, the group said in a statement.
"The Cuban contract will secure work for ADE's labour force and could mean an extra 180 jobs over the period of the contract," ADE managing director Ron Shires said.
"Possibilities of supplying the Cuban market with additional products and parts can be expected in the future," he added.

Shires said ADE had experienced a slow-down in local engine demand due to the reduction of import duties on commercial diesel vehicles but the company was showing strong growth in export contracts for diesel components in Europe, the U.S. and South Korea.
The company's export turnover on diesel components is expected to reach 160 million rand in the current financial year.
